title_en: Zhongyu Electronics (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Jiuying Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent
ruling_gist_en: The doctrine of prosecution history estoppel applies to amendments or statements that narrow the scope of patent protection. That is, the technical solutions thereby abandoned shall not be included back into the scope of patent protection. Such abandonment is usually a self-abandonment by the patentee through amendments or statements. However, if the independent claim is declared invalid and the patent is maintained valid based on its dependent claims, and the patentee has not made such self-abandonment, then full attention should be paid to the situation where the patentee has not self-abandoned, and the criteria for determining abandonment should be strictly applied. If the additional technical features in the dependent claim are not encompassed by the independent claim, then because these additional technical features have no original reference, it cannot be presumed that all technical solutions other than these additional technical features have been abandoned.
keywords_en: Civil; Dispute over infringement of utility model patent; Retrial; Supreme People's Court; Shanghai Municipality; Legal person; Patent Law; Application of the doctrine of prosecution history estoppel; Determination of the scope of patent protection; Determination of abandonment after maintenance of validity of dependent claims; Reversal of judgment; Utility model patent infringement; Steering gear product; Patent invalidation declaration; Doctrine of prosecution history estoppel; Clarifying the conditions for applying the doctrine of prosecution history estoppel; Unifying the standards for determining patent infringement; Patent right; Application for retrial; Intellectual property; Dispute over infringement of utility model patent
full_text_en:
Zhongyu Electronic (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Jiuying Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent

[Ruling Summary]

The doctrine of estoppel applies to amendments or statements that narrow the scope of patent protection. That is, the technical solutions thus surrendered should not be re-incorporated into the scope of patent protection. Such surrender is usually a voluntary surrender by the patentee through amendments or statements. However, if the independent claim is declared invalid and the patent is maintained valid on the basis of its dependent claim, and the patentee has not made the aforesaid voluntary surrender, full attention should be paid to the situation where the patentee has not voluntarily surrendered, and the conditions for determining surrender should be strictly applied. If the additional technical features in the dependent claim are not encompassed by the independent claim, since there is no original reference for such additional technical features, it cannot be presumed that all technical solutions other than such additional technical features have been surrendered.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 306

Petitioner for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Zhongyu Electronic (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 960 Shenglong Road, Jiufu Economic Development Zone, Jiuting Town, Songjiang District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Tian Yu, General Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Xue Qi, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Zhiyue Xinwen Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Xie Bing, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Zhiyue Xinwen Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shanghai Jiuying Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 98 Pengfeng Road, Malu Town, Jiading District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Huang Guochuan, Chairman of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Ding Hua, Attorney at Law, Shanghai Allbright Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Zhao Guohong, female, Han nationality, born July 23, 1952, patent agent of Beijing Zhuoyan Intellectual Property Agency, domiciled at No. 403, Gate 1, Building 9, No. 3 Xinjiekou Outer Street, Haidian District, Beijing.

The petitioner for retrial, Zhongyu Electronic (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongyu Company), in the case of a dispute with the respondent, Shanghai Jiuying Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiuying Company) over infringement of a utility model patent, was dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2010) Hu Gao Min San (Zhi) Zhong Zi No. 53 rendered by the Shanghai High People's Court and applied to this Court for retrial. This Court rendered the Civil Ruling (2011) Min Shen Zi No. 397 on August 1, 2011, granting the retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on October 26, 2011. Agents ad litem of Zhongyu Company, Xue Qi and Xie Bing, and agents ad litem of Jiuying Company, Ding Hua and Zhao Guohong, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

In August 2009, Zhongyu Company filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, alleging that: On February 13, 2008, the patentees Tian Yu and Jiang Wenyan were granted a utility model patent for "A Servo" by the State Intellectual Property Office, with patent number ZL200720069025.2. On February 10, 2009, Zhongyu Company and the patentees entered into a Patent Implementation License Contract, stipulating that Zhongyu Company was granted the exclusive right to use the said utility model patent with the authorization of the patentees, and the term of the exclusive license is valid until April 17, 2017. In February 2009, Zhongyu Company discovered at the International Nuremberg Spring Toy Fair in Germany that Jiuying Company was promoting a model aircraft of the model "FreeSpiritMicroNER/C210A" at the fair, and the servo used in such model aircraft fell within the scope of protection of the patent. Zhongyu Company entrusted an attorney to send a letter to Jiuying Company requesting it to immediately cease the infringing act, but Jiuying Company ignored it. In June 2009, Zhongyu Company discovered that Jiuying Company exhibited the patent-infringing product at the 6th Shanghai Model Aircraft Exhibition and sold such products in bulk at prices far below the cost of the patented product. In addition, Jiuying Company also promoted and marketed the infringing product through various means, including its company website and product catalogs. Jiuying Company, without the permission of the rights holder, used the utility model patent without authorization and sold infringing products at low prices, and continuously promoted the infringing products for a long time, seriously damaging the legitimate interests of Zhongyu Company. Therefore, Zhongyu Company requested the court to order Jiuying Company to: 1. immediately cease selling the infringing products, recall and destroy all infringing products; 2. destroy all molds for the infringing products, printed promotional materials, and delete the information on the infringing products on its website; 3. compensate Zhongyu Company for its economic losses including reasonable expenses in the amount of RMB 5 million (reasonable expenses include attorney fees of RMB 100,000, appraisal fees of RMB 20,000, notarization fees of RMB 3,000, and industrial and commercial investigation fees of RMB 95).

Jiuying Company argued that the technology used in its products is identical or not substantially different from the prior art and common knowledge, and thus does not constitute infringement of the "A Servo" utility model patent. It requested the court to dismiss Zhongyu Company's claims.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, at first instance, found the following facts: Tian Yu and Jiang Wenyan are the patentees of the utility model patent named "A Servo" (hereinafter referred to as the patent-in-suit), with patent number ZL200720069025.2, filing date of April 17, 2007, and grant announcement date of February 13, 2008. Claims 1-3 as announced in the grant of the patent-in-suit are: "1. A model servo, characterized by comprising a bracket, a motor, a lead screw, and a slider, wherein the bracket comprises a motor mount and a slider mount, the motor is disposed in the motor mount, a driving gear is provided at one end of the motor, the lead screw longitudinally passes through the slider mount, a driven gear is provided at one end of the lead screw, the driving gear and the driven gear mesh with each other, the slider is threaded on the lead screw, and the slider protrudes from the slider mount, and a brush is provided on the bottom surface of the slider. 2. The servo according to claim 1, characterized in that a fixing hole for fixing to a servo driving circuit board is provided on the bracket. 3. The servo according to claim 2, characterized in that a strip-shaped carbon film and silver film are printed on the servo driving circuit board, the bracket is fixed to the servo driving circuit board through its fixing hole, and the brush on the bottom surface of the slider contacts the carbon film and the silver film."

On February 10, 2009, Tian Yu and Jiang Wenyan entered into a Patent Implementation License Contract with Zhongyu Company, granting Zhongyu Company an exclusive license to implement the patent-in-suit in China. The license contract was recorded with the State Intellectual Property Office on March 24, 2009. On April 20, 2009, Jiuying Company filed a request for invalidation of the patent-in-suit with the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Reexamination Board). On July 22, 2009, the Patent Reexamination Board issued the Invalidation Request Examination Decision No. 13717 (hereinafter referred to as the No. 13717 Invalidation Decision), declaring claims 1-2 and 4-6 of the patent-in-suit invalid, and maintaining the patent right effective on the basis of claim 3. Dissatisfied with the decision, the patentees Tian Yu and Jiang Wenyan filed an administrative lawsuit with the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, which rendered the Administrative Judgment (2009) Yi Zhong Zhi Xing Chu Zi No. 2726 on March 10, 2010, upholding the No. 13717 Invalidation Decision.

On June 6, 2009, the agent of Zhongyu Company, under the supervision of a notary public, purchased a model aircraft from the booth of Jiuying Company at the Shanghai Exhibition Center, obtained a receipt, three name cards, and two copies of promotional materials, and took photos of the booth and the purchased aircraft. The Huangpu Notary Public Office of Shanghai, based on the application of Zhongyu Company, notarized the process of preserving the above evidence and issued the Notarial Certificate (2009) Hu Huang Zheng Jing Zi No. 4855. On September 1, 2009, the agent of Zhongyu Company, under the supervision of a notary public, logged into the website of Jiuying Company (URL: www.nineeagle.com) and saved and printed the relevant Chinese and English web pages and linked images on the company's introduction, product description, sales network, etc. The Dongfang Notary Public Office of Shanghai, based on the application of Zhongyu Company, notarized the process of preserving the above evidence and issued the Notarial Certificate (2009) Hu Dong Zheng Jing Zi No. 9766. On September 8, 2009, Tian Yu and Jiang Wenyan commissioned the Shanghai Intellectual Property Judicial Appraisal Center to conduct an appraisal on whether the technical features of the model aircraft servo manufactured and sold by Jiuying Company are identical or equivalent to those of the patent-in-suit. The appraisal conclusion was that the technical features of the model aircraft servo manufactured and sold by Jiuying Company are equivalent to those of the patent-in-suit.

In addition, based on the application of Jiuying Company, the court of first instance commissioned the Science and Technology Intellectual Property Affairs Center of the Ministry of Science and Technology (hereinafter referred to as the IP Affairs Center) on November 11, 2009 to conduct an appraisal on whether the technical features of the model aircraft servo produced and sold by Jiuying Company are identical or equivalent to the technical features of claim 3 of the patent-in-suit, and whether the technical features of the model aircraft servo produced and sold by Jiuying Company belong to the prior art. The IP Affairs Center issued the Guo Ke Zhi Jian Zi [2010] No. 09 "Judicial Expert Opinion" on March 16, 2010, stating: 1. Technical features a-f of the accused infringing product are identical to technical features A-F recorded in claim 3 of the patent-in-suit, and technical feature g of the accused infringing product is equivalent to technical feature G recorded in claim 3 of the patent-in-suit. 2. Technical feature a of the accused infringing product is identical to technical feature A' of the prior art solution (LS series proportional control servo produced by WES-Technik, Germany), which is "comprising a bracket, a motor, a lead screw, a slider, and a circuit board containing a servo driving circuit"; technical feature B' of the prior art solution only shows that the bracket includes a slider mount, no obvious motor mount structure is found, nor is a fixing hole on the circuit board containing the servo driving circuit found, but the difference in the way the bracket is arranged on the circuit board belongs to a direct replacement of habitual means in the relevant technical field, i.e., technical feature b of the accused infringing product has no substantial difference from technical feature B' of the prior art solution; in technical feature c of the accused infringing product, the motor is arranged on the circuit board via a motor mount, while in technical feature C' of the prior art solution, the motor is directly arranged on the circuit board, and this difference in the way the motor is arranged belongs to a direct replacement of habitual means in the relevant technical field, i.e., technical feature c of the accused infringing product has no substantial difference from technical feature C' of the prior art solution; technical feature d of the accused infringing product is identical to technical feature D' of the prior art solution, which is "the lead screw longitudinally passes through the slider mount, and a driven gear is provided at one end of the lead screw"; technical feature e of the accused infringing product is identical to technical feature E' of the prior art solution, which is "the driving gear and the driven gear mesh with each other"; technical feature f of the accused infringing product includes "a brush is provided on the bottom surface of the slider", while technical feature F' of the prior art solution is not directly disclosed, but a person skilled in the art can easily conceive, based on the directly recorded content of the prior art document and common knowledge, that the prior art solution implicitly includes the feature of "a brush is provided on the bottom surface of the slider", therefore technical feature f of the accused infringing product has no substantial difference from technical feature F' of the prior art solution; technical feature g of the accused infringing product is "a strip-shaped carbon film and gold-plated copper strip are printed on the circuit board containing the servo driving circuit, and the brush on the bottom surface of the slider contacts the carbon film and the gold-plated copper strip", while the prior art document does not directly record this technical feature, but implicitly includes a linear potentiometer, and the specific structure of such a linear potentiometer belongs to common knowledge, therefore technical feature g of the accused infringing product has no substantial difference from common knowledge, and a person skilled in the art, without creative labor, can adopt a specific structure with no substantial difference from common knowledge in the linear potentiometer implicitly included in the prior art solution.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held at first instance that the focus of the dispute in this case is whether Jiuying Company's prior art defense is established. First, it must be determined whether the prior art provided by Jiuying Company is prior art relative to the patent-in-suit, i.e., technology that was publicly disclosed in publications at home or abroad, publicly used domestically, or otherwise made known to the public before the filing date of the patent-in-suit. The LS series proportional control servo produced by WES-Technik, Germany, provided by Jiuying Company, was already publicly disclosed in the 2005 Issue 4 of "Aero Model," which predates the filing date of the patent-in-suit, April 17, 2007, so Jiuying Company may rely on it for a prior art defense. Second, the comparison of the technical features of the accused infringing product with the prior art should be limited to a single prior art solution, and may be combined with technical common knowledge of a person skilled in the relevant art. Based on the "Judicial Expert Opinion" of the IP Affairs Center, technical features a, d, and e of the accused infringing product are identical to technical features A', D', and E' of the prior art solution, respectively; technical features b, c, and f of the accused infringing product have no substantial difference from technical features B', C', and F' of the prior art solution, respectively; and technical feature g of the accused infringing product has no substantial difference from common knowledge. The court of first instance held that Zhongyu Company's claims that the appraisal procedure of the IP Affairs Center was illegal, the appraisal method was erroneous, and the appraisal conclusion was vague lacked factual and legal basis and were not accepted, and confirmed the "Judicial Expert Opinion" in accordance with the law. The technical solution of the accused infringing product is a simple combination of a prior art and common knowledge, Jiuying Company's prior art defense is established, and the accused infringing product does not constitute infringement of the patent-in-suit. In accordance with the provisions of Article 56, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2000), the court rendered the judgment: Dismiss Zhongyu Company's claims. The court acceptance fee for first instance was RMB 46,800, the litigation preservation fee was RMB 5,000, and the judicial appraisal fee was RMB 60,000, totaling RMB 111,800, to be borne by Zhongyu Company.

Dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, Zhongyu Company appealed to the Shanghai High People's Court.

The Shanghai High People's Court confirmed at second instance that the facts found in the first-instance judgment were substantially accurate. It also found that the Beijing High People's Court issued the Administrative Judgment (2010) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 705 on July 23, 2010, dismissing the appeal and upholding the original judgment.

The Shanghai High People's Court held at second instance that claims 1 and 2 of the patent-in-suit were declared invalid, and the patent right was maintained effective on the basis of claim 3. The scope of protection of dependent claim 3 is defined by the additional technical features of claim 3 ("a strip-shaped carbon film and silver film are printed on the servo driving circuit board, the bracket is fixed to the servo driving circuit board through its fixing hole, and the brush on the bottom surface of the slider contacts the carbon film and the silver film"), the additional technical features of claim 2 from which claim 3 depends ("a fixing hole for fixing to a servo driving circuit board is provided on the bracket"), and all the technical features recorded in claim 1 from which claim 2 depends. The reason dependent claim 3 was maintained effective is that the additional technical features recorded in dependent claims 2 and 3 were added to claim 1, which essentially amounted to amending claim 1 by adding the additional technical features of dependent claims 2 and 3 to the technical solution recorded in claim 1. Therefore, among the technical features defining the scope of protection of claim 3, "a fixing hole for fixing to a servo driving circuit board is provided on the bracket" and "a strip-shaped carbon film and silver film are printed on the servo driving circuit board, the bracket is fixed to the servo driving circuit board through its fixing hole, and the brush on the bottom surface of the slider contacts the carbon film and the silver film" are technical features added due to the restrictive amendment to the claims to maintain the patent valid. Thus, it can be determined that technical feature G of claim 3 (a strip-shaped carbon film and silver film are printed on the servo driving circuit board, and the brush on the bottom surface of the slider contacts the carbon film and the silver film) is a technical feature added due to the restrictive amendment to the claims to maintain the patent valid. According to Article 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Disputes, where a patentee, during the invalidation procedure, abandons a technical solution through amendments to the claims, and later includes it in the scope of patent protection in a patent infringement dispute, the people's court shall not support it. In this case, technical feature G of the patent-in-suit specifically limits the conductive strip of the linear potentiometer on the servo driving circuit board to "silver film". This specific limitation should be regarded as the patentee having abandoned technical solutions using conductive materials other than "silver film" as the conductive strip. Technical feature g of the accused infringing product is "a strip-shaped carbon film and gold-plated copper strip are printed on the circuit board containing the servo driving circuit, and the brush on the bottom surface of the slider contacts the carbon film and the gold-plated copper strip". According to the appraisal opinion of the IP Affairs Center, technical feature g of the accused infringing product is equivalent to technical feature G of the patent-in-suit. This determination by the IP Affairs Center was accepted by both parties, and there were no sufficient facts or reasons to overturn it, so it should be adopted. Although technical feature g is equivalent to technical feature G, according to the doctrine of estoppel, since technical solutions using conductive materials other than "silver film" as the conductive strip are deemed to have been abandoned by the patentee, the conclusion that the accused infringing product constitutes equivalent infringement cannot be established based on the equivalence of technical feature g and technical feature G. The first-instance court's conclusion that equivalent infringement was established was erroneous and should be corrected.

The prior art defense involves comparing the technical solution of the accused infringing product with the prior art solution. Whether the consistency of the structure of the "LS series servo" published in the 2005 Issue 4 of "Aero Model" with the patent-in-suit can be determined is not the issue that the prior art defense is concerned with. The servo sample provided by Jiuying Company at first instance was also not the prior art relied upon by the court of first instance in upholding the prior art defense. Therefore, this ground of appeal by Zhongyu Company cannot be sustained.

A prior art document's disclosed technical content shall be determined based on the technical content that a person of ordinary skill in the art can obtain from the corresponding technical document. Such technical content includes not only the technical content explicitly recorded in the technical document but also the technical content that can be directly and unquestionably determined from the technical document, which is what the Intellectual Property Affairs Center's "Judicial Appraisal Opinion" refers to as the "implicitly" disclosed technical content of the prior art document. Although the photograph and corresponding textual description of the servo disclosed in the 2005 Issue 4 of "Model Airplane" do not directly show a brush on the bottom surface of the servo slider, the appraisal experts of the Intellectual Property Affairs Center, based on the knowledge and experience of a person of ordinary skill in the art (including common general knowledge in the art), considered that a person of ordinary skill in the art, based on the photograph and corresponding textual description of the servo disclosed in "Model Airplane", could ascertain that "Model Airplane" disclosed that a brush was provided on the bottom surface of the servo slider. That is, the technical solution disclosed in "Model Airplane" implicitly includes the technical feature of "a brush is provided on the bottom surface of the slider," and therefore, further determining that there is no substantial difference between technical feature f of the accused infringing product and prior art feature F' is not improper. Similarly, although the photograph and corresponding textual description of the servo disclosed in "Model Airplane" do not directly show the conductive strip and resistive strip required for forming a linear potentiometer on the servo drive circuit board, the appraisal experts of the Intellectual Property Affairs Center, based on the knowledge and experience of a person of ordinary skill in the art (including common general knowledge in the art), considered that a person of ordinary skill in the art, based on the photograph and corresponding textual description of the servo disclosed in "Model Airplane", could ascertain that the servo disclosed in "Model Airplane" has a linear potentiometer. Thus, they effectively determined that in the servo disclosed in "Model Airplane", its drive circuit board has the conductive strip and resistive strip required for forming a linear potentiometer, and the brush on the bottom surface of the slider contacts the resistive strip and conductive strip; that is, the technical solution disclosed in "Model Airplane" implicitly includes the technical feature of "on the circuit board containing the servo drive circuit, a strip-shaped resistive strip and a conductive strip are printed, and the brush on the bottom surface of the slider contacts the resistive strip and conductive strip." They further determined that there is no substantial difference between technical feature g of the accused infringing product and prior art feature G', which is not improper. Zhongyu Company's corresponding appellate argument that the Intellectual Property Affairs Center's appraisal method does not respect facts and cannot rely on "implicit" inferences is untenable.

In the Intellectual Property Affairs Center's "Judicial Appraisal Opinion," the appraisal experts, from the perspective of a person of ordinary skill in the art, based on the technical solution disclosed by the photograph and corresponding textual description of the servo in the 2005 Issue 4 of "Model Airplane" (including technical content that cannot be directly seen but that a person of ordinary skill in the art can directly and unquestionably determine from the photograph and corresponding textual description based on their knowledge and experience, including common general knowledge), determined that the prior art defense in this case was established. However, the court of first instance considered that the "Judicial Appraisal Opinion" found the prior art defense established based on a simple combination of the technical solution disclosed by the photograph and corresponding textual description of the servo in the 2005 Issue 4 of "Model Airplane" with common general knowledge in the art. This is inconsistent with the actual reasoning of the "Judicial Appraisal Opinion" and should be corrected.

In summary, Zhongyu Company's appellate requests and reasons lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed. Moreover, even if Zhongyu Company's appellate reason that the prior art defense is not established could be sustained, this case would not constitute equivalent infringement due to the application of the prosecution history estoppel doctrine, and Zhongyu Company's claim that the accused infringing product in this case constitutes patent infringement would also not stand. Zhongyu Company's appellate request should also be dismissed. In accordance with Articles 6 and 14, Paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows: Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 46,800 shall be borne by Zhongyu Company.

Zhongyu Company, dissatisfied with the second-instance judgment, applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: (1) The court of second instance's determination that Jiuying Company did not constitute equivalent infringement based on the prosecution history estoppel doctrine was an error in applying the law. The patentee did not abandon any technical solution by amending the patent claims, nor by making statements in the opinions, and the patentee never stated in any patent application document that "only carbon film and silver film can be used on the servo drive circuit board." Therefore, Zhongyu Company's claim that Jiuying Company infringed the patent did not violate the prosecution history estoppel doctrine. Furthermore, even if the patentee had abandoned a technical solution, it would only have been technical solutions other than "carbon film and silver film directly printed on the servo drive circuit board," and did not include the technical solution defined by claim 3 of the patent-in-suit or the technical solution defined by "gold-plated copper strips" equivalent to "silver film." (2) The evidence materials relied upon by Invalidation Decision No. 13717 and the Intellectual Property Affairs Center's "Judicial Appraisal Opinion" are substantively the same. The only difference is that the former includes the evidence "Potentiometer Basics and Its Applications," while the latter includes the English version "The Potentiometer Handbook," which is a one-to-one translation. Therefore, Invalidation Decision No. 13717 upheld claim 3 of the patent-in-suit as valid, which was subsequently maintained by administrative judgments. This proves that claim 3 of the patent-in-suit possesses novelty and inventiveness over the prior art. However, the court of second instance, based on the appraisal conclusion of the Intellectual Property Affairs Center, determined that the accused infringing technical solution equivalent to claim 3 of the patent-in-suit constituted prior art, leading to two contradictory determinations on the same legal fact. Since Jiuying Company could not prove claim 3 invalid in the invalidation proceeding, using the same evidence to support a prior art defense is clearly untenable. Zhongyu Company requests this Court to: 1. Set aside the original judgments; 2. Order Jiuying Company to cease production and sale of the infringing products, recall all infringing products, and destroy them; 3. Order Jiuying Company to compensate Zhongyu Company for losses of RMB 5 million; 4. Order Jiuying Company to bear the first and second-instance litigation costs.

The respondent Jiuying Company argued: (1) Zhongyu Company, in the invalidation proceeding of the patent-in-suit, explicitly limited the conductive strip of the linear potentiometer on the servo drive circuit board to "silver film" through statements in the opinions. The Patent Reexamination Board accordingly determined that claim 3 possessed inventiveness and maintained it valid. That is, the patentee had effectively amended the claims to abandon technical solutions using other conductive materials as conductive strips besides "silver film." Additionally, the patentee had explicitly limited the conductive strip of the linear potentiometer to "silver film" in the specification, which allowed claim 3 to be granted. This limiting statement is consistent with the statements made in the invalidation proceeding and formed the basis for the inventiveness of claim 3. (2) The invalidation proceeding of the patent-in-suit and the civil judgment made by the court of second instance in this case involve different legal facts or legal relationships, and the evidence materials relied upon are different. The court of second instance correctly determined that Jiuying Company's prior art defense was established. The Intellectual Property Affairs Center's "Judicial Appraisal Opinion" was obtained through a lawful appraisal procedure, and its conclusion is correct and should be adopted. The "implicit inference" appraisal method complies with relevant laws and regulations. Jiuying Company requests this Court to dismiss Zhongyu Company's retrial application.

This Court, upon trial, finds that the facts found by the courts of first and second instance are substantially correct.

This Court, upon trial by the Retrial Division, considers that the focal issues disputed by the parties in this case are: (1) Whether the Patent Reexamination Board's decision to maintain the validity of the patent-in-suit based on claim 3 leads to the application of the prosecution history estoppel doctrine. (2) Whether Jiuying Company's prior art defense is established.

Regarding the first focal issue.

First, the legal basis of the prosecution history estoppel doctrine. The principle of good faith, as a fundamental principle of civil law, requires civil subjects to keep their promises and not harm the reasonable reliance or legitimate expectations of bona fide third parties, thereby balancing the potential imbalance caused by the free exercise of rights. In patent prosecution practice, patent applicants often narrow claims or specifications to obtain rapid grant but then attempt to re-include the abandoned technical solutions into the scope of patent protection through the doctrine of equivalents in infringement litigation. To ensure the stability of the scope of patent protection and protect the public's reliance interests, the patent system uses the prosecution history estoppel doctrine to prevent patentees from "having it both ways." Therefore, if a patentee abandons a technical solution through amendments to claims or specifications or statements in opinions during patent prosecution or invalidation proceedings, and then seeks to include that technical solution within the scope of patent protection in a patent infringement dispute, the people's court shall not support it.

Second, the conditions for applying the prosecution history estoppel doctrine. Generally, only amendments to claims or specifications or statements in opinions can lead to the abandonment of a technical solution, thereby triggering the application of the prosecution history estoppel doctrine. In this case, independent claim 1 and its dependent claim 2 were both declared invalid, and the validity of the patent-in-suit was maintained based on dependent claim 3, which depends from claim 2. The question is whether claim 3 alone constitutes a restrictive amendment to claims 1-2 from which it depends. When an independent claim is declared invalid and the patent is maintained valid based on its dependent claim, that dependent claim effectively replaces the position of the original independent claim. However, the content of that dependent claim or the scope of protection it defines does not change because the original independent claim was declared invalid. This is because each claim is a separate and complete technical solution, and each claim should accurately and completely define the scope of protection sought by the applicant in the original application, regardless of whether it appears as an independent claim. Therefore, each claim can be independently maintained valid or declared invalid. The validity of each claim shall be presumed to be independent of the validity of other claims. Even if the claim from which a dependent claim depends is declared invalid, that dependent claim cannot be considered invalid as a result. Therefore, the scope of protection defined by a dependent claim should not be considered restricted simply because the claim from which it depends is invalidated. The judgment of the court of second instance in this case, which held that claim 3 was maintained valid because additional technical features from claim 2 and claim 3 were added to claim 1, which essentially amended claim 1, is somewhat improper.

Third, the standard for determining abandonment. The scope of patent protection is defined by the technical features contained in the claims. Therefore, changes in the scope of patent protection are reflected in changes in the technical features of the claims. During patent prosecution or invalidation proceedings, the patentee, voluntarily or at the examiner's request, may limit the scope of protection defined by a claim by adding technical features or may provide a limiting interpretation of a claim through statements in opinions. The prosecution history estoppel doctrine applies to amendments or statements that result in a narrowing of the scope of patent protection, i.e., technical solutions abandoned thereby. Such abandonment is usually self-abandonment by the patentee through amendments or statements. However, if the Patent Reexamination Board finds the independent claim invalid and maintains the patent valid based on its dependent claim, and the patentee has not made such self-abandonment, then in determining whether there is "abandonment" for the purposes of the prosecution history estoppel doctrine, full attention should be paid to the situation where the patentee did not self-abandon, and the conditions for finding abandonment should be strictly applied. If the additional technical features in the dependent claim are not encompassed by the independent claim, then because there is no original reference point for those additional features, it cannot be presumed that all technical solutions outside those additional features have been abandoned. In this case, Jiuying Company argued that because claims 1-2 were declared invalid, and claim 3 is a further limitation thereof, the "territory" between claims 1-2 and claim 3 is presumed to have been abandoned. This Court considers that "silver film" in claim 3 was not mentioned in claims 1-2, and Zhongyu Company did not amend the claims or specification during the patent prosecution and invalidation proceedings, nor did it abandon technical solutions using other conductive materials as conductive strips besides "silver film" in its statements in opinions. Therefore, it should not be considered based on claims 1-2 being declared invalid that the additional technical feature "silver film" of claim 3 can no longer be subject to the doctrine of equivalents.

In summary, the Patent Reexamination Board declared claims 1-2 and 4-6 of the patent-in-suit invalid and maintained the patent valid based on claim 3. The court of second instance considered that technical feature G in claim 3 was essentially an additional technical feature added by amending the claim, and this feature explicitly limited the conductive strip to silver film, which should be regarded as the patentee abandoning technical solutions using other conductive materials as conductive strips besides "silver film." Consequently, it determined that the accused infringing product did not constitute equivalent infringement. This finding was erroneous and should be corrected.

Regarding the second focal issue.

Comparing the accused infringing technical solution with the technical solution of the "LS series proportional control servo" disclosed in the 2005 Issue 4 of "Model Airplane" magazine, the differences are: (1) The bracket includes a motor seat; (2) The motor is set within the motor seat; (3) A brush is provided on the bottom surface of the slider; (4) On the circuit board containing the servo drive circuit, a strip-shaped carbon film and gold-plated copper strip are printed, and the brush on the bottom surface of the slider contacts the carbon film and gold-plated copper strip. Regarding distinguishing technical features (1) and (2), although the motor seat is not shown in the prior art, using a motor seat to fix the motor is a common practice in the art, and these two technical features have no substantial difference from the accused infringing technology. Regarding distinguishing technical feature (3), although the prior art did not disclose this technical feature, in the structure of a servo, generally installing a brush at the bottom of the slider as the sliding contact of the potentiometer is a common practice in the art, and the book "Potentiometer Basics and Its Applications" also describes a potentiometer with a brush. Therefore, this technical feature has no substantial difference from the accused infringing technology. Regarding distinguishing technical feature (4), the prior art does not disclose this specific circuit board structure. Although Figure 2-7(a) of the book "Potentiometer Basics and Its Applications" discloses a potentiometer structure including a conductive strip, a strip-shaped resistive element, and a ceramic substrate, judging from the picture, the conductive strip does not correspond to the gold-plated copper strip in the accused infringing technical solution, and its resistive element and conductive strip are fixed on the ceramic substrate. However, the accused infringing product does not have an independent potentiometer; instead, the carbon film and gold-plated copper strip are directly printed on the drive circuit board, which functions to improve the integration of the servo, simplify the servo structure, reduce the weight of the servo, and achieve miniaturization of the model aircraft. It can be seen that this technical feature is not disclosed by the compared prior art, nor is it a technical feature that a person of ordinary skill in the art could directly or unequivocally derive from the prior art based on common general knowledge. Therefore, the accused infringing technical solution is substantially different from the prior art solution. The judgment of the court of second instance, which based on the appraisal opinion of the Intellectual Property Affairs Center determined that Jiuying Company's prior art defense was established, was erroneous and should be corrected.

Since both parties agree that distinguishing technical features g and G between the accused infringing technical solution and the patent-in-suit are equivalent technical features, and the prosecution history estoppel doctrine does not apply in this case, the accused infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. Furthermore, because Jiuying Company's prior art defense cannot be established, Jiuying Company constitutes infringement of the patent-in-suit and shall bear civil liability for cessation of infringement according to law. Since Zhongyu Company did not provide evidence to prove its losses or the profits gained by Jiuying Company from the infringement, and there is no patent license fee to refer to, this Court, taking into account factors such as the patent-in-suit being a utility model patent, the limited duration of the infringing activity, the role of the patent-in-suit in the product, and the reasonable expenses incurred by Zhongyu Company for investigating and stopping the infringement, determines the amount of compensation in this case to be RMB 200,000 by discretion. Since Zhongyu Company did not provide evidence to prove the inventory of the accused infringing products, specialized production molds, and written or website promotional materials, its related claims are not supported.

In summary, the judgment of the court of second instance finding that Jiuying Company did not infringe the patent-in-suit was an error in applying the law and should be corrected. In accordance with Article 11, Paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China as amended in 2000, Articles 21 and 22 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases, and Article 186, Paragraph 1 and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2010) Hu Gao Min San (Zhi) Zhong Zi No. 53 of the Shanghai High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2009) Hu Er Zhong Min Wu (Zhi) Chu Zi No. 167 of the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court;

2. Shanghai Jiuying Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. shall compensate Zhongyu Electronics (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. for economic losses in the amount of RMB 200,000 within fifteen days from the date of service of this judgment;

3. Dismiss the other claims of Zhongyu Electronics (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed payment shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 46,800, litigation preservation fee of RMB 5,000, judicial appraisal fee of RMB 60,000, and the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 46,800 shall all be borne by Shanghai Jiuying Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
